 SPOKANE, Wash. — The No. 15 Gonzaga Bulldogs (1-0) will host the New Mexico State Aggies (1-0) for the 2026-27 home opener at the McCarthey Athletic Center.
 Tipoff is set for 2 p.m. from The Kennel, with the game airing on NonStop Local KHQ.
 This will be the second all-time meeting between the Zags and Aggies, with Gonzaga winning the lone previous matchup 80-68 on Dec. 7, 2013.
 ABOUT NO. 15 GONZAGA 
 Gonzaga enters this game after defeating the Purdue Boilermakers 78-72 at the TNT Sports Hall of Fame Series in Las Vegas in its season-opening matchup.
 Sophomore guard Davis Fogle led the Zags in scoring against the Boilermakers with 22 points on 6-of-18 shooting from the field while converting on 9 of 10 free throws and adding 5 rebounds.
 Fifth-year guard Xavian Lee made a big splash in his first regular-season action for Gonzaga, going for 18 points, 4 rebounds and 3 assists on 4-of-7 shooting, including 3-of-4 from 3-point range.
 Fifth-year forward and Naismith Trophy Preseason Watch List nominee Braden Huff contributed 10 points and a team-high 7 rebounds, while newcomer Izan Almansa added 11 points and 4 boards against the Boilermakers.
 Overall against Purdue, Gonzaga shot 43.4% (23-of-53) from the floor but came to life from beyond the arc in the second half, shooting 37.5% (6-of-16) from 3-point territory in a game that featured nine lead changes.
 The Zags' defense made it difficult for the Boilermakers to find a rhythm from 3-point range, as Gonzaga held Purdue to just 12.5% (1-of-8) on 3s in the second half and 23.8% (5-of-21) overall.
 After the win over Purdue, Gonzaga ranks 13th overall, with the 11th-ranked offensive rating and 19th-ranked defensive rating according to the 2026-27 Ken Pomeroy College Basketball rankings.
 ABOUT NEW MEXICO STATE 
 New Mexico State enters the matchup after a season-opening 73-66 win over Western New Mexico.
 Senior guard and Okinawa, Japan, native DJ Dudley led the Aggies over Western New Mexico with 22 points, 5 rebounds and 3 assists on 7-of-14 shooting and 4-of-8 from 3-point range. Sophomore 6-foot-8 forward Mark Lavrenov racked up a 17-point, 10-rebound double-double in the game for the Aggies.
 In the 2025-26 season, New Mexico State went 16-16 and lost to Sam Houston in the second round of the Conference USA Championship. The Aggies entered this season picked to finish sixth in the CUSA preseason poll.
 New Mexico State is led by fourth-year head coach Jason Hooten, who holds a 46-50 (.479) overall record. Hooten spent the previous 13 years as the head coach of Sam Houston, where he amassed an overall record of 261-169 (.607).
 The Aggies enter this matchup as KenPom's 131st overall ranked team, holding the 169th-ranked offensive rating and 105th-ranked defensive rating.
